name: Learn beekeeping basics
blurb: Keeping bees is a genuine commitment with real responsibilities — disease reporting, swarm control and neighbours. Start with a local association, not a mail-order hive.
gear: Full suit, smoker and hive tool
A hive, and a legal, sensible location
steps: Join a local association and get a mentor before buying anything. Beekeeping is learned at the side of an experienced keeper.
Learn the colony: queen, workers, drones, the brood cycle and what a healthy frame looks like.
Learn to open a hive calmly: smoke lightly, move slowly, and keep inspections short.
Learn to spot the queen, or at least eggs, and to read the frames for stores and brood pattern.
Learn swarm control, which is your responsibility to your neighbours as much as to the colony.
Learn the notifiable diseases and pests in your region and your legal obligations to report them.
tips: Bees need year-round management and winter feeding. They are livestock, not an ornament.
Check for allergy in your household before starting, and never site a hive where the flight path crosses a neighbour’s garden.
proof: You take a colony through a full season under mentorship, including a successful overwintering.
